 Early voting for December 12 election begins November 28 in Bossier Parish
 November 18, 2026 November 18, 2026 / JSLLC 
 Early voting for the Saturday, December 12, 2026 election in Bossier Parish will run from Saturday, November 28 through Saturday, December 5 , giving registered voters an opportunity to cast their ballots ahead of Election Day.
 Key Dates & Voting Information 
 Online Voter Registration Deadline: Saturday, November 21, 2026 (The in-person and by-mail registration deadlines passed on November 12.) 
 Early Voting Period: Saturday, November 28 – Saturday, December 5, 2026
 Absentee Ballot Request Deadline: Tuesday, December 8, 2026, by 4:30 p.m. CST
 Absentee Ballot Return Deadline (by mail or in person): Friday, December 11, 2026, by 4:30 p.m. CST
 Election Day: Saturday, December 12, 2026
 Bossier Parish Sample Ballot (December 12, 2026) Note: Actual ballot items vary by municipality and district. Contests and propositions appearing on the Bossier Parish December 12 ballot include: 
 Parishwide Tax Propositions: 
 Proposition No. 1 (Health Units Millage Renewal): Renewal of the 0.82-mill property tax for 10 years (2028–2037) to construct, equip, and operate parish health units
 Proposition No. 2 (Roads & Bridges Millage Renewal): Renewal of the 1.99-mill property tax for 10 years for parish roads and bridges
 City of Shreveport Municipal Contests (for eligible Bossier Parish voters residing within Shreveport city limits) :
 Mayor: Tom Arceneaux (Republican) vs. Stormy Gage Watts (Democrat)
 City Court Judge, Election District 2, Division D: Kharmen Davis-Taylor (Democrat) vs. Sheva Sims (Democrat)
 Voters can confirm all municipal, district, and local propositions specific to their address on their personalized sample ballot. 
 Where to Vote Early in Bossier Parish Early voting locations can differ from Election Day precincts. Voters in Bossier Parish can confirm their designated early voting site, daily operating hours, and local Registrar of Voters contact details through the Louisiana Secretary of State’s GeauxVote Voter Portal or by contacting the Bossier Parish Registrar of Voters office in Benton. 
 What to Bring Voters casting a ballot in person are asked to bring an acceptable form of photo ID: 
 A Louisiana driver’s license or Louisiana special ID card
 A LA Wallet digital driver’s license
 A U.S. military identification card containing your name and picture
 Another generally recognized picture ID containing your name and signature
 (Voters who are unable to provide photo ID may still cast their ballot by signing a voter affidavit at the polls.) 
 Voters can review their personalized sample ballot, check their registration status, and confirm their Election Day polling place through the Louisiana Secretary of State’s GeauxVote Voter Portal or by contacting the Bossier Parish Registrar of Voters.
